items.prompt: In a video transcoding system, a media workflow must start a rendition job. large work must survive worker replacement without blocking interactive requests The design review focuses on workload shape, traffic patterns, and growth assumptions. The same mechanism appears in a different domain with one constraint changed. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: large work must survive worker replacement without blocking interactive requests
Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
The primary decision is model workload shape and growth assumptions before sizing the critical path..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Model workload shape and growth assumptions before sizing the critical path. In this transfer case for video transcoding, peak shape, read/write ratio, fan-out, and growth determine where capacity and buffering pressure appear. The owner must also make a worker dying during a long job observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide workload shape, traffic patterns, and growth assumptions independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a worker dying during a long job as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Model workload shape and growth assumptions before sizing the critical path. It addresses large work must survive worker replacement without blocking interactive requests through an explicit mechanism and keeps a worker dying during a long job inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Peak shape, read/write ratio, fan-out, and growth determine where capacity and buffering pressure appear. The transfer case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For video transcoding, the decision keeps large work must survive worker replacement without blocking interactive requests attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a worker dying during a long job as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Workload shape, traffic patterns, and growth assumptions” to terminology recall. Separate product requirements and quality targets from implementation choices; estimates must drive decisions rather than decorate the answer. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce workload shape, traffic patterns, and growth assumptions must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to Amazon SDE II Interview Prep (https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/sde-ii-interview-prep); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.
